Raghu
------------------------------------------
A famous king of the Sūryavaṁśa (lineage from Sun-god) and a distinguished scion of the इक्ष्वाकु race, he was the great-grandfather of Śrī राम. After him, the race itself came to be known as Raghuvaṁśa.
After conquering the whole world, रघु performed the विश्वजित् sacrifice wherein he had to give away all his wealth and possessions. When the sacrifice was over, the sage Kautsa (a disciple of विश्वामित्र) approached him for a very heavy गुरुदक्षिणा (fees to be given to the preceptor). Seeing the indigent circumstances of the king himself, Kautsa was about to depart. However, रघु dissuaded him and started preparing to attack कुबेर, the god of wealth, who rained gold coins on अयोध्या, the capital city. Kautsa took what he wanted, and left after blessing the king profusely.

Rāghavendratīrtha
(A.

-1671)
------------------------------------------
One of the brightest स्तर्स् of द्वैत Vedānta philosophy after मध्वाचार्य (A.

-1317) was Rāghavendra Tīrtha popularly known as ‘Rāyaru’ in Karnataka.
Born to Vīṇā Timmaṇṇabhaṭṭa and Gopamma as their last child—by the special grace of Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirupati—he was named Veṅkaṭabhaṭṭa. Being extraordinarily intelligent, he mastered the scriptures at an early age. He also became proficient in playing on the Vīṇā (lute).
RāghavendratīrthaHe was married to Sarasvatīdevī and had a son, Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, from her.
Later on, Suddhindratīrtha (16th century A. D.), the pontiff of a Mādhva मठ (monastery of the द्वैत tradition), under whom Veṅkaṭabhaṭṭa had got higher एदुचतिओन्, gave him सṁन्यास (monastic order) and appointed him as his successor. His monastic name was Rāghavendra-tīrtha.
During his long tenure as the next pontiff (from A.

to 1671) he contributed a lot to the spread of द्वैत Vedānta through his scholarly compositions, disputations and discourses. He had unique yogic powers which he liberally used to uplift those that badly needed succour.
In A.

, at the age of 76, he sat in deep meditation inside the बृन्दावन he had specially got prepared, which was filled up over his living body. He is believed to be still alive there, in his subtle body. This बृन्दावन is situated in the village, then known as Mañcāle, and now, as मन्त्रालय (See MANTRĀLAYA.).
It is claimed by his devotees that miracles are happening even now due to his presence and powers.
Some of his works—which total 48—are: Nyāyasudhāparimalā; Bhagavadgītā-vivṛti; Upaniṣatkhaṇḍārtha; Rāmacaritra-mañjarī and Kṛṣṇacaritramañjarī.

Raghunandana
(A.

-1580)
------------------------------------------
The Hindu way of life, technically known as आचार (conduct in daily life) and vyavahāra (social dealings) was largely determined by the smṛtis, the धर्म-śāstras and the निबन्धस् (digests).
The last group of works comprises encyclopaedic compositions by very scholarly and competent authors. रघुनन्दन was one such who lived in Bengal during the 16th century. He was the last of the great writers on the धर्मशास्त्रस्. His views on the various aspects of Hindu civil law are considered with respect even now, especially in Bengal.
Raghunandana was a vandyaghaṭīya ब्राह्मण from Bengal. His ड़थेर् was हरिहर-bhaṭṭācārya. His गुरु was Śrīnātha-आचार्य-cūḍāmaṇi.
According to the Bengali tradition, रघुनन्दन was a co-pupil of Śrī कृष्ण चैतन्य (A.

-1533) under वासुदेव Sārvabhauma. However, there is no confirmation of this from other sources.
Raghunandana’s magnum opus is the Smṛtitattva divided into 28 sections, also called tattvas. It is an encyclopaedic nibandha work on all aspects of धर्म-śāstras.
The Jīvānanda edition printed in A.

is in two volumes and has 1630 pages.
Some of the tattvas of this book are: Tithitattva, Śuddhitattva, Āhnikatattva, Śrāddhatattva, Prāyaścittatattva, Saṁ-skāratattva, Dāyatattva, Vyavahāratattva, Devapratiṣṭhātattva and so on.
His views on the शूद्रस् are very liberal. He has given them plenty of freedom in religious matters.
Raghunandana was a master in the application of the rules of the Mīmāṁsā philosophy and the न्यायस् or maxims, while discussing his subjects.
He is an authority on the दायभाग system of the division of property which is current in (and confined to) Bengal.

Raghunāthjī Temple
------------------------------------------
Situated in Jammu city, the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir State, the रघुनाथ्जी तेम्प्ले is the biggest temple complex of North India. It is actually a group of 13 temples, the 14th one—of Naṭarāja—having been added recently.
Inspired by and as directed by his गुरु, रामदास Bairāgī, Mahārājā Gulab Siṁha (Gulab Singh) the then king got the foundation stone laid in A.
. The temple complex was completed by his son, the next king, Mahārājā Raṇabīra Siṁha (Ranbir Singh) in A.

.
The sanctum of the main temple contains three beautiful marble images of Śrī राम, सीता and लक्ष्मण established on high सिṁहासन or throne. राम’s image is darkish in colour, the other two being white. The images are shown with the hand-pose indicating मङ्गल or auspiciousness.
Three of the interior walls are covered with gold sheets. The huge temple has seven śikharas or spires, each belonging to one deity or shrine. Subsidiary shrines are dedicated to various incarnations of विष्णु. There is a shrine for सूर्य or Sun-god also. A large image of हनुमान् adorns the entrance.
The complex contains eight enclosures called ‘ahātās’, each having a different name. Of them four named after the four Vedas—e.g., Ahātā Ṛgveda—are more important. They contain a large number of images of gods and goddesses as also of ‘Vibhīṣaṇa, सुग्रीव, विश्वामित्र, वाल्मीकि and others.
A very large number of Śivaliṅgas and sālagrāmas are also found located in these enclosures.
Behind the temple there is a huge tank covered over with an umbrella-like roof. The water of this tank is used for purposes of पूजा and other rituals.
Mahārājā Raṇabīra Siṁha had established a सṁस्कृत Mahāvidyālaya (Sanskrit College) which has now been taken over by the Central Government and renamed ‘Śrī Raṇabīr Kendrīya सṁस्कृत Vidyāpīṭha’. It runs a Pāṭhaśālā for teaching Sanskrit and various other traditional subjects like ज्यौतिष (Astro-logy) and कर्मकाण्ड (Vedic rituals) leading to diplomas and degrees.
The temple has a big library containing many valuable Sanskrit manuscripts.
The important festivals celebrated include रामनवमी, जन्माष्टमी and विजयदशमी.
Music programmes are organised during some festival days like Holī and वसन्तपञ्चमी.
Religious discourses are almost a daily affair.
